feedback: Written before this candidate has raced. Iteration 8 (±0.04 m row, kp 3.0, wheel_track 0.12 m) gave 36.3097, identical to iteration 6, so widening the row did not change the line-loss mechanism on the oval and s-bend. Iteration 7 (mass 0.5 kg) lowered the score to 35.64, so mass 0.8 kg is kept. Iteration 6 (kp 3.0) is the only change that has moved the score, and only on the slalom (14.39 to 45.18). The oval and s-bend still lose the line once, with max_error 0.061 m, which is just past the 0.06 m off-track floor. Your 0.10 m track is a yaw-response test, and iteration 3 showed a null effect at kp 2.0 with the narrower row. The combination with kp 3.0 and the ±0.04 m row is untested, so it is a fair test, but I make no claim about its outcome. The 0.10 m track raises yaw per unit turn, so slalom steering_oscillation is the risk to watch. Next-race rules: (a) if the metrics match iteration 8 or 6 to four decimals on all tracks, geometry is exhausted for this controller. Do not spend another iteration on geometry; move to kd near 0.2 with wheel_track 0.12 m. (b) If line_loss_events fall below one on the oval or s-bend, keep wheel_track 0.10 m and test kd near 0.2 to damp the slalom oscillation. (c) If line loss persists with max_error near 0.061 m but steering_oscillation rises above the 0.16 seen at wheel_track 0.12 m, the narrower track is over-steering. Keep the controller at kd 0.2 and do not change geometry further.
requested_changes: Hold the ±0.04 m, 16 mm row at y = 0.07 m with mass 0.8 kg and set wheel_track to 0.10 m. Iteration 8 (score 36.3097) is the baseline, and this race isolates wheel_track.

If the metrics match iteration 8 to four decimals, stop geometry changes. The next test is controller damping: kd about 0.2 at wheel_track 0.12 m, aimed at the slalom steering_oscillation of 0.16 seen in iteration 6.

If slalom steering_oscillation rises above 0.16 with zero line-loss change, keep the controller and test wheel_track 0.11 m as the midpoint. Iteration 3 gave no gain at 0.10 m with the narrower row, so do not go below 0.10 m.
